purpose: DL-055 evidence: confirms every alias authored in ch05-interconnection.json and ch07-state.json is the factually correct fully-qualified name in the real fixture source, and that sysml2d model_index.py (pinned commit 1af88250d355f4e218f6653ef934e93ac8319cd6) cannot resolve the correctly-qualified form -- only a truncated, package-prefix-dropped form that would be a wrong qualified name if used as an alias target.
root_cause: build_model_index pops package_stack/def_stack on every line starting with "}", regardless of whether a tracked keyword (package/part def/state def/action/state/interaction/use case) opened it. Both ch05.sysml and ch07.sysml contain an untracked brace pair inside action def ApplyHeat ("in duration : ISQ::DurationValue[0..*] { doc /* ... */ }", lines 16-20), whose closing "}" pops the real ApplyHeat action frame one line early; a later "assert constraint balance { ... }" (kind matched by the regex but not in the push-eligible set) then pops package_stack itself on its own closing "}", erasing the ToasterDemo package prefix before any part def / state def is reached.

interpretation.ch05.sysml: ToasterDemo::Toaster and ToasterDemo::Toaster::heating (the real, correct qualified names) are NOT resolved; the indexer only resolves the truncated, incorrectly-qualified Toaster / Toaster::heating forms.
interpretation.ch07.sysml: ToasterDemo::Cycle and ToasterDemo::Cycle::idle (the real, correct qualified names) are NOT resolved; the indexer only resolves the truncated, incorrectly-qualified Cycle / Cycle::idle forms.

conclusion: The aliases authored in ch05-interconnection.json / ch07-state.json are correct. The render/validate failures recorded in ch05-interconnection-sysmld-render.log, ch05-interconnection-sysmld-validate.log, ch07-state-sysmld-render.log, and ch07-state-sysmld-validate.log are caused by this indexer bug, not by an authoring error. Per ACE ruling DL-055, this is the Phase 0 finding for SysMLD on real fixture content, not a blocker to fix by mangling alias values to a technically-incorrect but indexer-friendly form.
